content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 7.2 (p0026) contains the document's only MFN provision, and it runs *against* us — we would have to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer before engaging another provider. It is open-ended (no defined product, no 12-month limit, no like-for-like carve-outs), so it fails all three fallback elements and reaches walk-away territory. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3's recital that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

**Redline (preferred level, validated ok:true):** a single surgical replace turning the prohibition/obligation operator around — "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives" — which removes the burden, cures the conflict with Section 12.3, and leaves any Vendor-granted MFN untouched. No cross-references to Section 7.2 exist elsewhere, so nothing dangles.
